direction.name: The split stage
direction.idea: Half the screen never moves. One side is a fixed photograph (or object, or product view) that stays in place for the whole visit; the other side is a calm scrolling column with everything you need to read. The fixed half keeps the feeling present while the reader gets on with the facts, like sitting in the room while reading the menu. As sections pass, the fixed image may quietly change to the one that matches.
direction.composition: Desktop: a two-column page, 50/50 or 45/55. One column is `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` and holds a single photograph filling it edge to edge, or the object centred on a flat field. The other column scrolls and holds all content in a single narrow measure (max 46ch) with comfortable padding (48–72px): name and one-line description first, then sections separated by generous space, then contact and footer. Headings in the scrolling column are modest (32–44px). The column grounds differ: photograph on one side, flat paper colour on the other, meeting at a clean vertical edge. On a phone the fixed half becomes a 60svh image at the top that stays sticky behind the first section, then releases.
direction.typography: A text-first setting: a readable serif or a calm sans at 17–19px, with one display size for the name. Left-aligned throughout.
direction.colour: The paper colour of the reading column is chosen against the photograph: a tone taken from its shadows or its lightest area. One ink, optionally one accent ink for links and the action.
direction.imagery: One excellent portrait-orientation photograph for the fixed half, plus three or four more that crossfade in as their sections arrive. Small inline photographs in the reading column are optional and should be few.
direction.richness: A full-height photograph always in view, against a quiet, well-set column of text.
direction.pitfalls: The reading column must be genuinely well typeset, since it is half the page. Do not put cards or grids in it. Check that the fixed image crops well at short viewport heights. In blind tests the commonest complaint was monotony: several screens of the same split with only the text changing. Change what the reading half holds from section to section (a list, a large figure, a table, a full-colour panel, a drawing) and let at least one section break the split and run full width.

hero.name: Striped card beside the room
hero.blueprint: The viewport is split 50/50 with a 12px gap and 12px outer margins. The right half is one full-height photograph of the room, corners radiused 16px, `position: sticky` so it stays in view while the left half scrolls. The left half is a printed card: a flat paper-colour panel with the same 16px radius, and the subject's stripe (from its awning, label or ribbon) as the only ornament. Across the card's top runs a band 56px tall made of alternating bars of the single ink colour and paper, each bar 28px wide, built as a flex row of filled blocks. The same stripe returns as an 8px band above the footer and inside the button on hover. Under the band, centred: the wordmark about 300px wide, then a two-line headline in a light serif at clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 56px) in the ink colour, one supporting sentence at 17px held to 36ch, and the single action as a solid rectangular button. Three text links sit in one centred row at 15px, 28px above the card's bottom edge. One ink on paper; the photograph supplies every other colour.
hero.mobile: The photograph comes first at full width inside 12px margins, 48svh tall, with the 16px radius. The card follows and overlaps the photograph's bottom edge by 24px using a negative margin. Its striped band is 40px tall; below it the wordmark at 56% width, the headline at 8vw on two lines, the sentence and the button, all centred. The links wrap into the card's foot.
hero.headline: A warm two-line welcome of three to six words, up to about 18 characters per line at 3.6vw.

type.note: A contemporary slab with smooth curves and unbracketed serifs, even enough to carry headings and paragraphs alike. Suits developer tools, personal sites, open-source and nonprofit projects.

palette.name: Three stones
palette.note: Three close stone tones share the interface: the lightest for the page, the middle one for panels, the darkest for a single band, all with charcoal type. Saturated colour is left to the photographs and their backdrops; the grey-green fills the button only.

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Plain names in columns
sections.blueprint: A typographic list with no logos. The heading, two or three words at 28–32px, sits in columns 1–3 and stays top-aligned with the first row of names. Columns 5–12 hold the names in three or four text columns (`columns: 4; column-gap: 32px`), each name on its own line at 20–22px with leading 1.5, sentence case, in the full ink. Where names fall into kinds (clients, press, partners), each kind starts a new column and its first line names the kind in the softer ink at the same size, so no small labels are needed. Columns are of unequal length and are not balanced; ragged bottoms are intended. Twelve to thirty names work best. There are no boxes, bullets or separators: the column edges and the shared baseline do the organising. Leave 120px above and below.
sections.mobile: The heading leads at 26px. Names follow in two columns at 17px with a 20px gap; each kind begins after a 32px break with its name in the softer ink on the first line. Long names wrap inside their column rather than shrinking.

sections.name: Itinerary on a slip
sections.blueprint: The process is printed as an itinerary or receipt. One paper-coloured slip 420–480px wide stands on a contrasting flat ground at columns 7–11; its bottom edge is a zigzag cut with clip-path and its top edge is straight. The heading, two to four words at clamp(40px, 4.4vw, 68px), sits in columns 1–5 with a 30ch paragraph, top-aligned with the slip. On the slip, in the text face at 16px with tabular figures: stages grouped under time headings that carry the order ('Monday', 'Midweek', 'Friday'), each heading in bold with 28px above it. Under a heading, two to four rows; each row has what happens on the left, a duration or time on the right, and a leader of round 4px dots between. The final row is inverted, paper-coloured text on a full-width ink bar 44px tall, and states the result: what the reader holds at the end and the total time.
sections.mobile: The heading and paragraph come first. The slip follows at full width minus 16px margins, keeping its zigzag bottom edge. Rows keep left text, dots and right value on one line; long descriptions wrap under the left text. The inverted final row stays full width.

sections.name: Pinned heading, passing rows
sections.blueprint: One flat saturated field, full-bleed, as tall as its content. Columns 1–5: the heading, two or three words, at clamp(56px, 6.6vw, 104px) in the heaviest weight, position: sticky; top: 32px, so it holds while the right side travels. Columns 7–12: four to six capability blocks stacked with 120px between them. Each block is a title at 28px bold, then a two-part row: a portrait photograph at 3:4, 180–220px wide with square corners, and beside it, top-aligned, a plain list of four to six short lines at 18px with 14px between lines. Photographs alternate between the left and the right of their list, so the column does not read as a ladder. One ink colour, chosen for contrast on the field. The heading releases when the bottom of the last block reaches it.
sections.mobile: The heading becomes a sticky bar at the top of the section: one line at 9vw on the field colour with 12px padding, holding while blocks pass under it. Each block stacks its title, a full-width 4:3 photograph, then the list at 17px. 72px between blocks.

sections.name: Portrait and offset quotation
sections.blueprint: A 12-column row on the page ground with wide margins. A portrait of the speaker, 3:4, fills columns 2–5 and is tall, about 70svh; it takes whatever mask the page gives its photographs (square corners, or the page's one motif shape). The quotation occupies columns 7–12 and starts 120px lower than the top of the portrait: four to six lines at clamp(26px, 2.6vw, 40px) in a light or regular weight, leading 1.2, measure about 26ch. The name and role sit 32px beneath the quotation at 16px, on its left edge. A second, small photograph (1:1, columns 10–11) hangs 96px below the attribution and shows the place or the thing the speaker is talking about. There is no heading. Nothing is centred; every edge lands on a column line, and the two vertical offsets are the design.
sections.mobile: The portrait runs at 72% width from the left margin, 3:4. The quotation follows at 24px, full width, starting 32px beneath. Name and role sit under it. The small second photograph sits at 44% width against the right margin, 48px lower, overlapping nothing.

sections.name: Answers as reading text
sections.blueprint: The questions and answers are set as continuous reading text, like the notes at the back of a programme. A heading of two or three words at 28–32px sits in columns 1–3, top-aligned. Columns 5–12 hold the text in two columns (`columns: 2; column-gap: 56px`), each about 36ch wide, at 16–17px with leading 1.55. Each item is one paragraph: the question is the opening run-in, set in the medium weight in the full ink and ending with its question mark, and the answer continues on the same line in the regular weight. Paragraphs are separated by 20px and carry `break-inside: avoid` so none splits across columns. No toggles, no icons, no boxes. Eight to fourteen items fit on one screen, which is the point: everything is answered at a glance. Where the page's reading column is narrow, use one column.
sections.mobile: One column at 16px with 20px margins. The heading leads at 24px. Each paragraph keeps its run-in question in the medium weight, with 18px between paragraphs. The section may run to two screens; do not collapse it into an accordion.

sections.name: Last photograph, text beside
sections.blueprint: A final full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 90svh, chosen so its subject sits in the left half and its right half is calm. All text is confined to the right half and never crosses the centre line: in columns 8–12, anchored to the lower third, a closing line of three to five words at about 3.4vw in a light weight, a paragraph of two or three lines at 17px, and one filled button in the paper colour with ink text, about 52px tall. If the image behind the text is not calm enough, darken the whole photograph slightly with `filter: brightness(0.8)` rather than laying a panel behind the words. The section butts directly against a footer in one solid colour, so the photograph's bottom edge is a hard line. No logo, no second action.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 100vw by 70svh, cropped to keep its subject. The text leaves the image and sits beneath it on the footer's solid colour: closing line at 28px, paragraph at 17px, full-width button. Image and colour meet at a hard edge.

sections.name: Photograph half, menu half
sections.blueprint: A split footer one viewport tall. The left half is a single photograph filling columns 1–6 edge to edge, cropped hard by the left and bottom viewport edges: a close crop of the page's main subject, larger than it appeared anywhere above. The right half, on a flat field, is the site's menu set large: five or six section names stacked as links at about 2.6vw bold, 28px apart, starting at column 8 and 80px from the top. Rows are separated by space only; on hover a row's label shifts right by 12px and the others drop to the softer ink. Under the menu, 64px lower, two short blocks at 15px side by side: contact and social. The legal line runs along the very bottom of the right half at 12px. The wordmark sits small at the top of the right half, on the menu's left edge.
sections.mobile: The photograph leads at full width and 50svh, cropped tight. The menu follows on the flat field at 8vw per item with 20px between items, then contact and social stacked at 15px, then the legal line at 12px. The wordmark sits small above the menu.

references.name: Le Petit Bleu
references.idea: The cafe's teal-and-white stripes become the whole system: one teal ink on cream, everything boxed in thin double outlines like printed menu cards, beside a permanently visible photo of the room.
references.hero: Viewport split 50/50 with 12px gaps. Left: a cream panel with a thin pale-teal outline and rounded corners. Inside, a second outlined box is the nav bar: two-line hamburger left, teal brush-script logo about 300px wide centred, a caps order link right. Below, a two-line light serif headline at about 3.5vw, centred, in teal, then two centred stacks, each a bold caps label, a serif line and a solid teal button wrapped in a second thin outline. Right: a full-height rounded photo of a striped booth, with an outlined hours bar across its top, three slide dots bottom-left and a white address card bottom-right.
references.type: Self Modern, a light bookish serif, for headline and 15px body; Matter SQ bold caps for labels and buttons; Archive Mono Pro typewriter caps for menu rows; a brush-script logo. Section titles are tall condensed serif caps sized so four to seven letters fill the column.
references.colour: #fcfbf7 #13a7b2 #058599 #cfe5e7 #e9b81f — Cream paper and a single teal used for every word, rule, outline and button; no black anywhere. Yellow, floral reds and marble enter only through the interior photographs.
references.imagery: Bright, saturated interior and food photographs; the right-hand panel is a full-height slideshow with rounded corners. Small food shots sit in a horizontal strip, and a fine line drawing of the shopfront with one teal awning fills a card.
references.layout: The left half scrolls as a stack of outlined cream cards (full-width or two-up) with 12px gaps while the right half stays fixed. Card contents are centred. A sticky nav card rides over the stack. On mobile the photo becomes the hero card's background.

sections.description: A card containing only the section word in tall condensed serif caps, teal, sized so its four letters fill the column edge to edge. Below it, a stack of full-width outlined rows about 36px high, each with a category name in typewriter mono caps at left and a thin plus sign at right, separated by 6px gaps. Above the title: a ticker row of tiny caps and a strip of four small food photos with rounded corners.

The same giant condensed title treatment, then centred serif paragraphs in teal with underlined links in a narrow measure of about 280px. Further down, a landscape photo of the two proprietors with a centred two-line caption in tiny sans, followed by more centred paragraphs. All of it lives in the left half while the right photo panel has advanced to a shelf-wall image.

A header row with a tiny bold caps label at left and a script follow-us link with arrow at right, then three portrait images (about 3:5) with 12px rounded corners in a row, the third cropped by the column edge to imply a carousel. Directly below, the next giant section title begins and is cropped by the viewport.

steal: Print everything in one brand ink on cream, including body text, rules and buttons, and let photographs supply the other colours.
Wrap buttons and panels in a second thin outline offset by a few pixels to get a printed-ticket feel.
Keep a tall photo panel fixed on one half and scroll a stack of cards on the other, swapping the photo as sections change.

references.name: Rafael Derolez
references.idea: A portfolio as a phone carousel: a fixed text rail on the left narrates whichever phone-shaped screen is centred on the right.
references.hero: Dark charcoal page split by a vertical hairline at 30% width. Left rail: a 55px header row with name, slash and current section as a breadcrumb in 16px sans, plus a small cobalt ticket-shaped hire button with a perforated divider and arrow; below a hairline, four short paragraphs of 16px grey text with white links, top-aligned, leaving the lower 40% of the rail empty. Right 70%: three phone-proportioned frames with large rounded corners in a row; the centre one upright, full brightness and about 680px tall, the outer two smaller, dimmed and rotated in perspective toward the centre.
references.type: Suisse at a single 16px size, weight 400, for everything; hierarchy comes only from grey versus white and from the breadcrumb. The one larger setting is a bold two-word line inside the blue contact card. No display type at all.
references.colour: #18181b #030303 #969696 #173ded #ffffff — Zinc-black field with grey text and white for links and the active breadcrumb. Cobalt blue appears only on the hire button and contact card; all other colour comes from the app screenshots.
references.imagery: Phone-shaped frames with large corner radius holding app screens, a selfie and short videos; side frames are dimmed to about 40% and tilted in 3D like a cover-flow.
references.layout: Single viewport, no page scroll: a fixed 432px text rail with 32px padding and a media stage filling the rest. Scrolling advances the carousel and replaces the rail's text; hairlines separate rail, header and stage. On mobile the stage stacks above the rail.

sections.description: Same two-part frame. The breadcrumb's last word changes to the project name; under the header sit three tiny grey meta tags (employer, platform), then two paragraphs. On the stage the centred phone shows the product screen at full brightness while neighbours show the previous and next items dimmed and tilted, so the carousel works as both navigation and preview.

In the rail, a cobalt card shaped like a ticket with notched sides: tiny labels top-left and top-right, a large bold two-word heading, name and local time in small text, then a perforated lower strip with email at left and a copy button at right. Under it, a career list: company in white with dates in small grey on one line, role on the next, and a small arrow at the far right of each row.

steal: Use a breadcrumb (name / current item) as the only heading and update its last word as the content changes.
Show work in device-shaped frames arranged as a cover-flow, with neighbours dimmed and tilted so the next item is always previewed.
Shape the contact card like a ticket with notches and a perforated strip so the one accent-colour element feels like an object.

references.name: ARCHIV
references.idea: A waitlist page as a museum plinth: one cut-out everyday object at a time, centred on off-white beneath a heavy serif wordmark.
references.hero: Off-white single screen with no scroll. A heavy high-contrast serif wordmark in black caps sits top-left at a 56px margin, about 410px wide (28% of the viewport) and 80px tall. Opposite, top-right at the same margin, one line of 14px sans description aligns with the wordmark's top. Dead centre, one photographed object (a painted wooden pepper mill about 140px wide and 440px tall) stands on a barely visible lighter rounded square with a soft contact shadow; other objects replace it in turn. Below, a centred 11px grey line, then a white rounded email field 236px wide with a circled arrow inside its right end. Roughly 80% is empty.
references.type: The wordmark is drawn lettering in a heavy display serif with tight spacing, cap height about 5.5vw. All live text is Helvetica Neue regular at 14px and about 11px, black or grey. Two text sizes only; the contrast is wordmark against near-invisible interface text.
references.colour: #f1efec #000000 #ffffff #d9261c #e8a317 #7a7a75 — Warm off-white field, black wordmark, a white input; all colour arrives through whichever object is showing (red and yellow mill, tan leather, blue cap).
references.imagery: Studio cut-outs of single everyday objects in three-quarter view with a soft grounded shadow on matching off-white, each scaled to similar visual mass and centred, one at a time, no frame.
references.layout: One fixed viewport with four elements: wordmark top-left, description top-right, object in the exact centre, form bottom-centre. Margins of 56px, no rules, nav or footer. On mobile the wordmark centres and the description disappears.

sections.description: The central object rotates through unrelated things (pepper mill, sling chair, sticker-covered hydrant, layered iced drink, record player, baseball cap), each photographed in the same light and replaced in place within a zone roughly 250-300px square. Shadow direction and visual weight stay constant, so the object is the page's only variable and no carousel controls are needed.

Beneath the object, a centred line of 11px grey text, a 30px gap, then a white field about 236 by 52px with 12px radius: light grey placeholder at left and a 26px circle-outlined arrow as the submit control inside the right end. No button label, border or shadow; the field is the only pure white on the page, which marks it as the one interactive thing.

steal: Build a pre-launch page from four elements only (wordmark top-left, one-line description top-right, a single centred object, an email field) and leave the rest of the screen empty.
Cycle one consistently lit cut-out object in the same spot to show range without adding a grid or carousel controls.
Make the email field the only pure-white element on an off-white page, with submit as a circled arrow inside it rather than a labelled button.
